task.description: Hard-gate CODE-DESIGNER's fix design for ISS-0396 (lib/letflow/design/iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md) against the real source, independently re-verifying the design's correction of the Step-1 diagnosis's reachable-trigger claim, key-disambiguator uniqueness/correctness, no-other-reader-of-old-key-shape, test adequacy, and the two open questions (OQ-1/OQ-2) under the project's no-silent-deferral standard.

result.summary:
All 7 checks pass. Design approved -- routing to Step 3 ELIXIR-DEV.

1) Key disambiguator: verified directly against task_activation.ex:242-276 (current 6-arg append_multi_from_existing_records/6, key `Multi.run(multi, {:task_records, instance_id}, ...)` at line 258) and sub_process.ex:944-972 (build_completion_write_steps/12's current 5-arg call site, no disambiguator). Design's proposed change (optional 7th param `key_disambiguator \\ nil`, defaulting to byte-identical old key; non-nil only at the one changed call site, producing `{:task_records, instance_id, parent_token.id}`) is a correct, minimal, additive change. Confirmed engine.ex's two other call sites are cited at their real line numbers: `maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7`'s 6-arg call at engine.ex:2674, and `persist_timer_fired_advance/7`'s inline 6-arg call at engine.ex:2009 -- both grep-confirmed to be the exact call sites, both untouched by the design.

2) parent_token.id uniqueness: independently re-derived the ACTUAL reachable trigger, not the design's narrative alone. Read engine.ex:572-605 (`prepare_sub_process_children/5`, the create/2 root-activation path) -- confirmed it has NO membership/persisted-token check, accepting every `{:sub_process_start, token_id, node_id}` unconditionally. Contrasted with engine.ex:2314-2380 (`prepare_sub_process_children_for_completion/8` + `resolve_parent_token_record_id/2`), which DOES reject any token_id not in `persisted_token_ids` (pre-existing before the hop chain began) with `{:sub_process_after_split_join_not_supported, token_id}`. Read the ISS-0067 test directly (test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs:922-970): it proves a same-hop-chain PARALLEL_GATEWAY split feeding SUB_PROCESS nodes via `complete_task/3` is rejected with zero children created and a full rollback -- independently confirming the design's correction that `complete_task/3` cannot produce 2+ prepared_children today, and that `Engine.create/2`'s root path (engine.ex:1085-1109, `build_sub_process_children_multi/6`) is the only currently-reachable trigger. Each sibling's parent_token resolves to a distinct TokenRecord UUID PK (dispatch_parallel_split/4 mints one branch token per split edge) -- uniqueness holds.

3) Read-your-own-writes: read `load_parent_context/2` in full (sub_process.ex:1070-1111) -- confirmed it issues fresh `Repo.get`/`Repo.all` reads at call time on the open transaction's connection, with no caching or staleness risk; sibling N's reads genuinely observe sibling N-1's already-applied writes. Key disambiguation is purely a Multi step-name change and does not touch this function's signature, body, or call order.

4) No other reader of old key shape: re-ran `grep -rn \":task_records\" lib/ test/` myself (not reusing the design's own grep output) -- confirmed exactly two production call sites (task_activation.ex:176, the fixed-atom `append_multi/6`, untouched; task_activation.ex:258, the tuple-keyed function this fix touches) and no other file pattern-matches either key shape. All other hits are design-doc/test-comment prose.

5) Test design: `graph_root_split_into_two_subprocesses/1` fixture and the Engine.create/2-based test body (§5) are precisely specified -- concrete graph shape, concrete assertions (no raise, parent :completed, 2 child_projections, 2 SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED events, 0 orphan tasks, incidental ISS-0397 join_counters cross-check) -- genuinely exercises the corrected root-activation trigger path, not the foreclosed hop-chain path. Adequate for TEST-DESIGNER to implement without further disambiguation.

6) OQ-1/OQ-2 (no-silent-deferral check): OQ-1 (future ISS-0067 relaxation) is correctly resolved in-doc already -- the fix lives at build_completion_write_steps/12, the convergence point for all three call sites, so no design change is needed regardless; this is not a deferral, it's a closed forward-compatibility note. OQ-2 (nested/no-join cascade variant) was left as a genuinely open question for CDV to confirm -- I independently investigated and RESOLVED it using material already in the design's own citation trail: read `find_matching_join/2` and `dispatch_parallel_split/4` in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:772-843. Confirmed a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split whose branches do not converge on a single matching join gateway is rejected at split-dispatch time with `{:error, {:no_matching_join_found, node.id}}`, aborting the transition before any such instance can ever execute. This forecloses OQ-2's premise (an 'unbalanced/non-block-structured split' variant reaching two independent completions with no join) categorically -- such a graph shape can never produce a running instance in the first place. OQ-2 is therefore moot, same conclusion class as OQ-1: no design change needed. This does not constitute a design defect requiring rework (the design named the exact resolving mechanism and correctly declined to assume it without verification); I record the resolution here rather than sending back for a prose-only update, since it does not change any code ELIXIR-DEV needs to write.

7) No implementation code: scanned every code fence in the design doc (grep for defmodule/defstruct/```) -- only an @spec block (lines 108-118) and a literal `grep` shell command shown as a fenced example (lines 213-215). No `.ex` function bodies present.

Conclusion: design is unambiguous, fully specified (including error shapes via the existing @spec + case clauses referenced), and requires no rework. Approved.
